Holding GT tokens may also grant benefits.Transaction feesInstant Buy/Sell Fee: Variable on card providerMaker fees: 0.09% - 0% based on 30-day trading volumeTaker fees: 0.09% - 0.02% based on 30-day trading volumeStaking: Variable fees deducted from rewardsLending: Variable fees deducted from rewardsDiscounts on trading fees for GT holdersDeposit/withdrawal feesCrypto deposits: Generally free, minimum deposits + network fees applyCrypto withdrawals: Varies on asset, minimum withdrawal + network fees applyCash deposit fees: Up to 3%Minimum deposit: From $10Cash withdrawal fees: Up to 3%Minimum withdrawal: From $10How this list was builtWe’ve reviewed the crypto exchanges with the lowest fees available globally, focusing on those that offer strong security and product versatility. The exchanges are not ranked from best to worst as each offers unique strengths, but for easier navigation, we’ve listed them by traffic volume as a proxy for popularity. All are reputable providers, but as with any investment, always DYOR before investing.Most cryptocurrency exchanges charge different fees depending on whether you're a market maker or taker:Taker fees: You’re a taker when you accept the current market price, and your order executes immediately. This removes liquidity from the exchange, so taker fees are usually higher.Maker fees: You’re a maker when you place an order that doesn't execute immediately, such as a limit order. This adds liquidity to the market, and as a result, maker fees are generally lower.Aside from trading fees, exchanges may charge for additional services:Withdrawal fees: Applied when transferring crypto off the platform.Deposit fees: Some platforms charge fees for depositing fiat currency.Fiat conversion fees: Common in fiat-to-crypto transactions, these fees can be significant.Subscription fees: Platforms like Coinbase One offer fee-free trading in exchange for a monthly subscription.Reducing your trading fees is possible with a few strategic actions:Increase trading volume: Many platforms offer fee discounts to users with high monthly trading activity.Use limit orders: Limit orders typically qualify for maker fees, which are lower than taker fees.Join VIP or subscription programs: Some exchanges offer reduced fees through paid subscriptions or VIP tiers.Pay with native tokens: Exchanges like Binance offer discounts if you pay fees using their native tokens (e.g., BNB).Are trading fees tax-deductible?Yes. Some trading fees can reduce your taxable gains:Buy transactions: Fees can be added to your cost basis.Sell transactions: Fees can be subtracted from your proceeds.However, do check the rules where you live, as there are limitations on which trading fees may be allowable.In many cases, yes. Decentralized exchanges (DEXs) typically charge lower trading fees, often between 0.1% and 0.5%; however, most DEXs don't have fiat on/off-ramp options. However, remember to account for blockchain gas fees, which can add to the cost. Tools like 1inch aggregate DEX pricing to help you find the most cost-effective trades.Don't forget the tax bill...Whatever exchange you're using, you'll need to pay tax when you trade or sell crypto on an exchange and make a gain, as well as potentially Income Tax on several other transactions like staking and other rewards. A crypto tax calculator like Koinly integrates with more than 900 exchanges, wallets, and blockchains to let you calculate your crypto taxes easily and quickly.
